answers.question: How long before I can run again? A friend wants me to race the Thanksgiving 10K in five weeks.
answers.answer:
Your first run is planned for Sat Oct 24, six days after the race. Only run it if stairs feel normal and the blister isn't changing how you land. Until then, walk and spin easy.

The week of Oct 26 brings short easy runs and no workouts. Most runners are back to normal training about three weeks after a marathon.

Yes, the Thanksgiving 10K on Thu Nov 26 fits. It falls about five and a half weeks after the marathon. That leaves two easy weeks first, then about three weeks with strides and one short faster session a week, easing off in the last few days.

We can decide in early November whether you race it flat out or run it as a strong fun run. How your easy runs feel by then will tell us. Also tell me whether it's a one-off with your friend or the start of a bigger goal.

new.analysis:
The taper week went exactly as planned. Every run hit its planned distance and both rest days were rest. Wednesday's marathon-pace reps held 8:34/mi with no fade, so there is nothing to correct.

You had the fitness for goal pace, but your legs ran out around 20 miles. You held a touch quicker than 3:45 pace through about 20.5 miles. After that you slowed by roughly a minute per mile.

| Stretch | Pace |
| --- | --- |
| Needed for 3:45 | 8:35/mi |
| First 20.5 mi | about 8:32/mi |
| Last 5.7 mi | about 9:28/mi |
| Whole race | 8:48/mi (3:50) |

Three things probably wore your quads down. The course climbed 617 ft, well over the 423 ft of your hilliest long run, and downhills load the quads hardest. Your long runs all stayed near 10:00/mi, and the race moving two weeks earlier cut your build to two 20-milers.

So next time the fix is durability, not more fitness. A full build would stretch the long run further, put marathon-pace miles inside some long runs, and add hills like the race course. Your easy runs held about 9:50/mi at 138 bpm all autumn, so sub-3:45 looks within reach.

This week is rest first and running second. Stairs are still hard, which means your quads are still recovering. Running on them now risks a strain that would cost more time than it saves, while walking and easy spinning keep you moving without adding load.

Next week stays easy too, and then the plan needs a direction. Expect three or four short easy runs during the week of Oct 26, with no workouts and no long run. From Nov 2 we can aim at the Thanksgiving 10K, start toward a spring marathon, or spend a few months building easy base.

safetyCallouts.title: Get sore spots checked if they turn sharp.
safetyCallouts.body: General soreness should ease a little each day. If pain settles in one spot, feels sharp, or is no better by Thu Oct 22, skip running and see a physio or doctor.

safetyCallouts.title: Keep an eye on the blister on your left big toe.
safetyCallouts.body: If it gets redder, warmer, swollen or more painful, have a doctor or pharmacist look at it before you run.
